Using JohnCRM

Knowledge Base

Give AI useful source material, choose who can receive it, and test answers with evidence.

On this page
Organise spaces and foldersAdd a note, file or websiteCheck source readinessChoose who can receive an answerTest an answer with evidence

Organise spaces and folders

Open Knowledge Base in the sidebar. Spaces group folders by who can receive their content; folders organise related documents, websites and API endpoints. The page opens an existing folder, or invites you to create the first one.

  1. 1Use Spaces in the toolbar to review your audience groups. Everyone is the default space for information available to all contacts.
  2. 2Use the plus button beside a space to add a folder. Name it for one subject, such as opening hours or booking policies.
  3. 3Open a folder’s menu to rename it or move it to another space. On a phone, open the tree from the toolbar to choose a folder.

Add a note, file or website

  1. 1Select a folder and use its add area. Choose Write a note, Upload files or Add a website; you can also drop files there.
  2. 2Write notes with clear headings and short question-and-answer pairs. Notes autosave; wait for the saved state before relying on the update.
  3. 3Upload supported documents such as PDF, Word or text files, or provide one public HTTPS page. Check the resulting status and extracted content.

Ready content can be used by AI replies without a separate publishing step. Keep policies current and use the wording your customers use. The tree filter finds source names; KB test searches the content used for answers.

Check source readiness

  • Processing means the source is being prepared. Ready means the AI can use it. Ready, with notes means some material was left out; open the explanation to review it.
  • Couldn’t read means the source is unavailable to AI. Follow the error guidance; for scanned PDFs, supply readable text if text extraction is unavailable.
  • Out of date means a website changed and the saved version is still in use. Refresh now replaces it. Auto check can detect future changes; editing saved website text pauses automatic checks.

Choose who can receive an answer

In Spaces, leave general information open to everyone or restrict a space to selected User Types. A contact with any selected type can receive answers from it. Untyped contacts and unknown visitors receive only open-space content. A restricted space with no selected types answers no contacts.

Review changes to access

Moving content to a more widely accessible space can expose it to more contacts. Review the audience confirmation before continuing. Managing sources, spaces and retrieval tests requires the appropriate knowledge-base management permission.

Test an answer with evidence

  1. 1Open KB test in the toolbar and ask a question exactly as a customer would.
  2. 2Choose the asking audience: Everyone, a User Type or a specific user. Check the answer, any handoff, and the source sections included or left out.
  3. 3Open a source result to inspect the exact section. Improve the source or its audience settings, then test again. Pin useful questions to repeat after content changes.
What a test uses

No customer is messaged and the rehearsal does not apply data changes. It does call read-only API endpoints when needed and uses your workspace’s AI credits. The test explains differences from a live conversation.

The right answer is missing

Check that the source is Ready, the selected asker can access its space, and the relevant section appears in the evidence. Update unclear or outdated text and test with the customer’s wording. If a result matched but was left out, inspect the reason shown before changing the AI’s instructions.
